COVERED.meaning: Rule is closed for ACS coverage: directly covered, indirectly covered, or no standalone ACS check is required. See Notes for the reason.

NOT_COVERED.meaning: Rule is not closed by ACS coverage. It is either not testable by ACS or is a coverage gap. See Notes for the reason.

rules.notes: Indirect: monitor001 programs request PARTID and PMG and verifies monitor accounting distinguishes the labels.
No ACS check required: MSC may implement zero or more resource controls. ACS checks controls only when discovered.
No ACS check required: MSC may implement zero or more monitors. ACS checks monitors only when discovered.
Direct: reg001 checks MPAM version EXT bit behavior.
Direct: reg004 checks MPAM-for-RME feature requirements.
No ACS check required: different MPAM architecture versions may coexist. ACS validates each discovered MSC against its advertised version.
No ACS check required: base memory behavior rules always apply. No separate SYS-MPAM ACS check is required.
Indirect: non-secure PARTID space is exercised by ACS. Secure, Realm, and Root spaces cannot be directly validated from Non-secure execution.
Not testable: ACS cannot compare the same PARTID across Secure, Non-secure, Root, and Realm PARTID spaces.
Not testable: ACS cannot access all PARTID spaces to prove each PARTID scope is space-local.
No ACS check required: Default PARTID 0 is architecturally defined; labeling non-MPAM requesters with it is permitted, not mandatory.
Not testable: ACS cannot observe non-MPAM requester labeling to prove Default PMG 0 is used.
Not testable: requester-generation mechanism is system-wide. ACS cannot prove every PE, SMMU, GIC, and non-PE requester path.
Not testable: non-PE requester-generated PARTID space, PARTID, and PMG values are not directly observable by ACS.
Not testable: non-MPAM requester default/system-specific labeling is not directly controllable or observable by ACS.
No ACS check required: terminating completer has no downstream MPAM propagation to observe. No ACS runtime check is needed.
Not testable: intermediate forwarding of MPAM information is fabric behavior. ACS cannot observe the downstream bundle directly.
Not testable: buffered-request MPAM retention is internal. ACS cannot force or inspect a buffered request path.
No ACS check required: conditional cache-internal storage rule. ACS checks observable controls and monitors when present.
Indirect: cache partition tests exercise MSC response to request MPAM information.
Indirect: partition tests exercise per-PARTID control lookup from request MPAM information.
Not testable: cache-line MPAM metadata is internal. ACS cannot inspect the PARTID associated with each line.
Not testable: cache eviction metadata is internal. ACS cannot prove PARTID preservation from inner to outer cache.
Indirect: reg001.c is used as a representative simple MMR access test. It uses the common MSC discovery/configuration path, including integrated PE MSCs if discovered.
Indirect: reg001.c is used as a representative Non-secure MMR access test. Secure, Realm, and Root PA spaces are not directly accessible to ACS.
Indirect: reg004/reg005 check visible MPAM-for-RME and four-space capability.
Indirect: reg004/reg005 cover visible PE/MSC capability; Non-secure traffic exercises Non-secure MPAM_SP propagation.
Indirect: reg001.c is used as a representative Non-secure MPAM access test. ACS cannot directly observe MPAM_NS signal propagation or Secure-side traffic.
Not testable: ACS cannot generate Secure traffic or check reserved Secure PARTID-space encodings.
Not testable: ACS cannot observe 4-to-2 bridge reduction from Root/Realm MPAM_SP to MPAM_NS.
Not testable: ACS cannot observe whether a 4-to-2 bridge uses static or dynamic reduction.
Not testable: ACS cannot observe 2-to-4 bridge expansion from MPAM_NS to MPAM_SP.
Not testable: ACS cannot prove bridge preservation of physical address space and PARTID space.
No ACS check required: design statement for true two-space components. No separate ACS runtime check is needed.
Not testable: mAP4SPTO2SP is Root PA-space only; Non-secure ACS cannot verify Root-only access.
Not testable: external mapping register is Root PA-space only; Non-secure ACS cannot verify Root-only access.
Not testable: ACS cannot observe fixed MPAM_SP to MPAM_NS bridge signal mapping.
Not testable: ACS cannot identify or control all non-MPAM components to prove they do not propagate MPAM information.
Not testable: ACS does not control SMMU-attached requester traffic or observe its PARTID-space use.
Not testable: completer interface behavior. ACS cannot observe whether MPAM information was dropped before a non-MPAM completer.
Not testable: interconnect transport behavior. ACS cannot directly observe MPAM information on fabric links.
Not testable: cache-line MPAM metadata is internal. ACS cannot inspect whether allocated lines store the request MPAM information.
Not testable: cache eviction propagation behavior. ACS cannot observe MPAM metadata passed with evicted cache lines.
Direct: CSUMON tests check cache-storage usage monitoring when implemented.
Direct: CSUMON PMG/PARTID filter tests check cache-storage accounting for matching criteria.
Not testable: write-hit cache-line association is implementation-specific and cache-internal; ACS cannot observe the chosen association.
No ACS check required: write-hit portion update is permitted but not required, so there is no mandatory ACS behavior to check.
No ACS check required: reset/default-state behavior. SYS-MPAM ACS does not need a runtime check unless MPAM controls are discovered after boot.
Direct: cache partitioning tests use CSU measurement to validate capacity-based partitioning behavior.
Direct: RIS tests exercise resource/control discovery and RIS-based control or monitor selection.
Direct: partitioning and RIS tests exercise common resource-control selection using PARTID and RIS.
Direct: RIS tests exercise resource-instance selection and RIS-based control/monitor behavior.
Indirect: RIS tests rely on discovered RIS values, but uniqueness is not the primary assertion.
Indirect: RIS tests use RIS values in the 0..RIS_MAX range, but sparse assignment is not the primary assertion.
Gap: common controls can only be inferred when advertised at RIS 0. If identical controls appear for all RIS values, ACS cannot prove whether they are common or per-resource.
Indirect: error009 exercises RIS no-control behavior, which covers unsupported non-zero RIS paths for partition controls.
Direct: monitor RIS tests use MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL.RIS to select resource-instance monitors.
Indirect: monitor RIS tests exercise RIS selection and unsupported monitor RIS paths; unassociated-monitor RIS 0 is not separately asserted.
Indirect: RIS tests use RIS_MAX and undefined RIS paths, but do not directly assert every permitted RIS decode rule.
Direct: RIS error tests validate undefined RIS, no-control, and no-monitor selected-resource cases.
Direct: error012 checks ID register HAS fields read zero and no ESR error for undefined RIS.
Not testable: virtual PARTID resolution happens before the MSC. ACS cannot observe the pre-resolution virtual PARTID path.
Direct: reg005 checks MSC four-space capability when MPAM for RME is supported.
Indirect: reg001.c is used as a representative MMR access test using MPAMF_BASE_ns from ACPI/platform data. Secure, Realm, and Root base fields are not validated.
No ACS check required: allows controls and monitors to differ by PA space. No standalone ACS check is required.
No ACS check required: defines when a resource can be partitioned. Actual controls are checked only when implemented.
No ACS check required: describes possible RIS support for multiple resources. No standalone ACS check is required.
No ACS check required: lists optional standard partitioning interfaces. ACS checks only implemented interfaces.
Indirect: partitioning tests check IDR support bits before exercising each advertised control.
Indirect: CPOR and MBWPBM tests use portion/PBM width and allocation behavior, but do not directly assert every generic portion property.
Indirect: feat001 exercises PARTID enable/disable behavior; the global-to-MSC scope is not directly asserted.
Direct: feat001 verifies that a disabled PARTID allocates no resource or receives the lowest priority.
Not testable: ACS cannot directly observe preserved hardware settings across PARTID disable/re-enable; behavior can only give indirect confidence.
Gap: needs a direct test to disable and re-enable one PARTID, then verify the effect across all RIS values.
Gap: needs a direct PARTID narrowing test that disables a request PARTID and verifies the enabled status controls request behavior.
No ACS check required: defines normal enabled-control behavior. Feature-specific tests cover the implemented controls.
Direct: reg006 checks NFU is not implemented when PARTID narrowing is supported.
Not testable: boot/reset enable state across all PARTIDs and spaces is not directly testable after firmware handoff.
Direct: partition001 checks cache portion partitioning.
Indirect: partition001 exercises PARTID-based cache portion allocation.
Indirect: partition001 programs CPOR through the generic portion-control model.
Indirect: partition001 exercises CPBM permission bits through CPOR allocation behavior.
Indirect: partition001 uses CPBM as the cache instance of the generic PBM model.
Not testable: cache-line portion after CPBM change is internal, and both reallocation and retained misallocation are allowed.
Direct: partition004 checks cache associativity partitioning.
Direct: partition002 checks cache maximum-capacity partitioning.
Indirect: partition005 compares CMAX with SOFTLIM disabled/enabled, but does not directly prove unused capacity cannot be used above CMAX.
Direct: partition005 checks CMAX soft-limit behavior.
Direct: partition006 checks CMIN allocation-priority behavior.
Indirect: feat001, partition005, and partition006 exercise priority inputs, but not as a standalone priority table check.
Indirect: cache partition tests exercise allocation behavior, but do not directly assert each candidate-selection step.
Direct: mem001 configures MBWPBM portions and validates bandwidth partition behavior with MBWU counters.
Direct: mem001 programs BWPBM bits through MBWPBM configuration and validates permitted bandwidth behavior.
Indirect: mem001 validates BWPBM behavior as a PBM-style bandwidth portion control.
No ACS check required: lists optional bandwidth partitioning methods. ACS checks only methods that are implemented.
Indirect: mem002 and mem003 validate MBWMIN/MBWMAX fraction behavior, but not every bandwidth control type in the table.
Not testable: end-to-end bandwidth guarantee across concatenated MSCs is system-performance behavior that ACS cannot prove reliably.
Direct: mem002 programs MBWMIN under contention and validates bandwidth behavior with MBWU counters.
Direct: mem003 programs MBWMAX hard limits and validates bandwidth behavior with MBWU counters.
Gap: needs a combined MBWMIN+MBWMAX test; current tests validate each control separately.
Indirect: mem002 and mem003 validate MBWMIN/MBWMAX behavior that relies on accounting-window tracking.
Not testable: accounting-window carry-over is internal and implementation-dependent; ACS cannot reliably prove unused bandwidth does not accumulate.
Not testable: fixed accounting-window state is internal; ACS cannot reliably prove history clear and new-window behavior.
Gap: priority partitioning for same-preference conflicts is testable, but no current mapped test covers it.
Not testable: moving accounting-window history aging is internal; ACS cannot reliably prove request aging and removal behavior.
No ACS check required: allows implementation-defined bandwidth tracking methods. No standalone ACS check is required.
No ACS check required: defines proportional stride as a generic proportional-control instance. No standalone ACS check is required.
Gap: hAS_PROP advertisement is testable through MPAMF_MBW_IDR, but no current mapped test covers it.
Gap: needs a combined proportional-stride + MBWMAX test; current tests cover MBWMAX only.
Gap: different priorities per MSC are testable through priority controls, but no current mapped test covers them.
Not testable: upstream QoS priority arrival is fabric behavior. ACS cannot observe incoming interconnect priority signals.
Not testable: priority override affects internal MSC operation and downstream transport priority; ACS cannot directly observe it.
No ACS check required: internal priority partitioning is optional even when downstream priority exists. No mandatory ACS check.
No ACS check required: downstream priority partitioning is optional even when internal priority exists. No mandatory ACS check.
Not testable: response priority is downstream-to-upstream fabric behavior. ACS cannot directly observe response priority preservation.
No ACS check required: implementation-defined controls cannot be interpreted generically by ACS. No standalone ACS check is required.
No ACS check required: PARTID narrowing support is optional. ACS checks narrowing behavior only if implemented.

No ACS check required: defines monitor types. ACS checks monitors only when the corresponding monitor type is implemented.
Indirect: PARTID-based monitor tests use request PARTID filters; narrowing-specific behavior is not directly proven.
Gap: top-level monitor RIS 0 access is testable, but no current mapped monitor test covers it.
Direct: MBWU tests count payload bytes during memory workloads using MBWU monitor filters.
Gap: mBWU capture-event behavior is testable if capture registers exist, but no current mapped test covers it.
Direct: MBWU overflow tests prefill the counter near maximum and verify overflow behavior.

Direct: intr004 prefills MBWU_L near maximum and verifies long-counter overflow status/interrupt behavior.
Gap: no current ACS test triggers a CSU capture event; reg003 only rejects prohibited overflow-capture capability.
Indirect: CSU and MBWU monitor tests read monitor VALUE only when NRDY is clear; no standalone structural check covers every monitor instance.
Indirect: MBWU tests verify VALUE advances/resumes and CSU tests read/write VALUE; no single test covers all VALUE-field behaviors.

Indirect: CSU monitor tests reprogram PMG/PARTID criteria on the same monitor and continue reading VALUE after new traffic.

Direct: MBWU monitor tests fail if the monitor remains not-ready after update/wait paths.
No ACS check required: automatic NRDY clear is not required for event monitors. No mandatory ACS check.

Direct: MBWU monitor tests wait MAX_NRDY_USEC and fail if NRDY remains set when the value is read.

Gap: needs capture-event tests across monitor instances and capture registers; current tests only check prohibited capture capability.

Gap: capture feature coverage is pending; no current ACS test verifies external capture distribution.
No ACS check required: capture reset after copy is permitted but not required. No mandatory ACS check.

Indirect: monitor007 verifies post-overflow counter freeze/advance behavior, but does not directly assert the wrapped VALUE.

Direct: monitor tests disable the monitor, update MSMON_CFG control/value state, and verify the written state is usable.
Direct: monitor007 checks configurable monitor overflow behavior.

Gap: capture feature coverage is pending; no current ACS test verifies capture events stay local to one MSC.
Direct: monitor008 checks overflow status reset when monitor VALUE is written.

Gap: capture feature coverage is pending; no current ACS test verifies local capture distribution across address spaces.

Gap: capture feature coverage is pending; current OFLOW_FRZ test does not verify freeze caused by a capture event.
Indirect: error014 triggers a second MPAM error after the first and verifies ESR updates, showing continued MSC error handling.

Direct: error014 generates a second MPAM error before clearing ESR and verifies ERRCODE updates.

Direct: error001 checks out-of-range PARTID_SEL error behavior.

Direct: error012 reads MPAMF_IDR with undefined RIS, and error013 reads MPAMCFG after programming undefined RIS.
Direct: error008 checks undefined MPAMCFG_PART_SEL.RIS access and accepts ERRCODE 8 or RAZ/WI behavior.

Direct: error005 checks out-of-range monitor selector error behavior.
Not testable: read value is architecturally UNKNOWN for out-of-range MON_SEL, so ACS cannot validate a required value.
Not testable: post-write behavior is implementation-defined with UNKNOWN selector or WI, so ACS cannot validate one required result.
Direct: error010 checks undefined RIS handling in MSMON_CFG_MON_SEL.

Indirect: implemented error tests exercise required reporting for selected supported error conditions.

No ACS check required: lists possible MPAM interrupt sources. ACS checks only implemented interrupt behavior.
No ACS check required: four-space MSC choice of Secure or Non-secure error interrupt is permitted. No mandatory ACS check.

No ACS check required: error interrupt type may be level-sensitive or edge-triggered. ACS checks the implemented type.
Direct: intr001 checks level-sensitive error interrupt behavior.
Gap: level-sensitive error interrupt must not use MSI. This is testable if interrupt type is discoverable, but no current mapped test covers it.
Direct: intr002 checks edge-triggered error interrupt behavior.

No ACS check required: overflow interrupt support is optional. ACS checks overflow interrupts only if implemented.

Direct: intr005 checks MSI overflow interrupt edge-triggered requirement.

Not testable: locks are per PARTID space. Non-secure ACS cannot verify locks in Secure, Realm, or Root spaces.

Not testable: monitor locks are per PARTID space. Non-secure ACS cannot verify locks in Secure, Realm, or Root spaces.
No ACS check required: implementation-defined MMRs are permitted above offset 0x3000. No mandatory ACS check.
Indirect: reg001.c is used as a representative MPAM feature-page register access test. Reserved/unimplemented register locations are not exhaustively probed.
Indirect: reg001.c is used as a representative Non-secure feature-page access test. Other PA-space feature pages are not accessible to ACS.
Indirect: reg001.c is used as a representative Non-secure feature-page base access test. Secure, Realm, and Root bases cannot be validated from Non-secure ACS.
No ACS check required: different feature-page base addresses are permitted and overlap avoidance is a recommendation. No mandatory ACS check.
Gap: feature-page alignment and containment are testable from platform data, but no current mapped test covers them.
No ACS check required: non-MPAM MMR placement in the feature page is permitted only for trapped MMRs. No mandatory ACS check.
Indirect: all SYS-MPAM MMR-based tests require the Non-secure MPAM feature page to exist.
Not testable: secure feature page existence cannot be verified from Non-secure ACS execution.
Not testable: realm and Root feature pages cannot be verified from Non-secure ACS execution.
No ACS check required: rO MMR sharing across security states is permitted when contents match. ACS cannot and need not check sharing.
Indirect: PBM partitioning tests program CPBM/MBWPBM words using IDR widths and PBM offsets.
Gap: unused PBM bits being RES0 is testable, but no current mapped test covers it.
Indirect: fractional partitioning helpers program values using percentage minus one lsb, and tests validate resulting behavior.
Direct: tests program 100 percent controls and disable PARTIDs through MPAMCFG_DIS.PARTID.
